who: Historian of modern China at the University of Chicago; PhD Yale, 2008.

evidence.says: The authority for Johanna S. Ransmeier cites Chicago's faculty website: PhD Yale 2008, with research in modern China, Chinese legal history and family history.
Chicago identifies Johanna Ransmeier as an associate professor in History and East Asian Languages and Civilizations, researching law and family life in modern China.
Stephanie Painter's dissertation acknowledgements explicitly identify Johanna Ransmeier as her advisor.

notes: The authority's fuller name, doctorate and field agree; Painter supplies a direct supervision link.

who: Military historian at Penn State; PhD University of Kentucky, 1987.

The 2010 center newsletter identifies Timothy Orr and his advisor Professor Carol Reardon, and reports Orr's May 2010 graduation.
The candidate's LC authority identifies the author of Soldiers and Scholars as the Penn State military historian with a Kentucky doctorate in 1987.

notes: Institution, doctorate and direct evidence for Orr identify the candidate; Gabriel's supervision was not separately checked.

who: Historian of disability and psychiatric institutions at York University; history PhD Toronto, 1997.

Carolyn Podruchny's CV lists Joanna Pearce's 2023 York history doctorate on experiencing blindness, co-supervised with Geoffrey Reaume.
York's faculty list includes Geoffrey Reaume and records his MA and PhD as Toronto degrees.

notes: The doctorate and field match the authority; Pearce provides direct confirmation of supervision at York.

who: Historian of Indigenous North America and the Pacific Northwest at the University of Washington; history PhD UC Davis, 2009.

evidence.says: Joshua L. Reid's CV records a UC Davis history PhD in September 2009, Washington employment from 2015, and doctoral advising of Alika Bourgette (2024) and Madison Heslop (2022), with the listed dissertation titles.
The authority identifies Joshua L. Reid as author of The Sea Is My Country, a former UC Davis history graduate student and history professor at Massachusetts Boston.

The alternative candidate J. Nicholas Reid teaches Old Testament and Ancient Near Eastern Studies at Reformed Theological Seminary, Orlando, and holds an Oxford DPhil in Oriental Studies with a cuneiform emphasis.

notes: Both students are explicitly confirmed in Joshua L. Reid's CV, which also connects the Massachusetts Boston and Washington appointments. Reject alternative p-19750: different doctorate, field and institution.

who: Historian of early modern French religious and social life at Boston College; PhD Princeton, 1985.

evidence.says: Boston College identifies Virginia Reinburg as a history professor with a Princeton PhD, specializing in early modern Europe, especially France, religion and the history of the book.
Boston College's history graduate brochure lists Virginia Reinburg, associate professor, with a Princeton PhD dated 1985.
The archival finding aid describes Reinburg as holding a Princeton PhD in 1985 and serving as an assistant professor at Boston College from 1985.
The LC authority identifies Virginia Reinburg of Boston College as author of French Books of Hours (2012).

notes: Name, institution, doctorate and research field agree; the faculty timeline covers the students' period. Individual supervision was not separately verified.

who: Historian of nineteenth-century US politics and the Civil War at Wisconsin–Milwaukee; PhD Virginia, 1991.

evidence.says: Wisconsin–Milwaukee lists Lex Renda as associate professor emeritus of history, with a University of Virginia PhD in 1991 and interests in US political and legal history.
The department reports more than thirty-three years at UWM before his 2025 retirement, and again gives his Virginia doctorate as 1991.
The authority for Lex Renda, author of Running on the Record, cites UWM's faculty website: associate professor of history, PhD University of Virginia, 1991.

notes: The authority and department agree on institution, degree and field; employment covers 2020–2021. Individual supervision was not separately verified.

who: Historian of North Dakota at the University of North Dakota, 1935–1970; PhD Western Reserve, 1936.

evidence.says: UND's Elwyn B. Robinson Papers finding aid records history department service from 1935 to 1970 and a Western Reserve PhD in 1936 on Philadelphia's Civil War press.
The authority identifies Elwyn B. Robinson, author of History of North Dakota, as a UND history professor with a Western Reserve PhD in 1936.

notes: The fuller name, institution and doctorate agree; the appointment covers both student years. Western Reserve is the historical institution name corresponding to the AHA's Case Western Reserve label. Individual supervision was not separately verified.
